mappings.rationale: Uraian-level match, not title-only: the 2025 uraian describes 'kegiatan produksi kayu bulat dari penebangan hutan' (roundwood production via forest felling) used either as input to wood-product industries or unprocessed (pit-props, fence posts, electricity/telephone poles) -- an active timber-extraction/logging activity. This is semantically distinct from the adjacent forestry families visible on the SAME lampiran page that DID consolidate: 'pemanfaatan kayu hutan' (plantation-utilization licensing regime, 2020 codes 02111/02112/02113/02119/02121/02122) all collapsed into the single 2025 code 02102, and 'pemungutan hasil hutan bukan kayu' (non-timber forest-product collection, 2020 codes 02301-02309) all collapsed into 02300. 02201 ('Pemanenan Kayu'/logging-harvest) sits structurally apart from both of those regimes and was NOT swept into a merge -- confirmed bidirectionally: BPS Vol.2 Lampiran 5 (2020->2025 forward, p.135) shows 02201->02201 as an isolated single row with no fan-out to other 2025 codes, and Lampiran 10 (2025->2020 reverse, p.329) shows the same isolated 02201<-02201 row with no other 2020 code contending for it. Both tables independently agree on a clean 1:1, and the title differs only in capitalization ('Pemanenan kayu' vs 'Pemanenan Kayu'), consistent with the semantic match rather than being the sole basis for it.

payload.notes: pp28/ layer = ABSENT.json (11,208 pages scanned across 21 PP28 source files, code 02201 not found in any rendered PP28 lampiran page). No KBLI-2020-vintage PP28 row exists to image-verify, so this is NOT a D2 licensing-inheritance case: canonical.json's per_skala licensing data traces to _l1_source=OSS_RBA_2025_id_version_fff4053d (a 2025-native source) and _l2_status=no_oss_risk, not to an inherited PP28 table. pp28_sources=["02201"] in canonical.json is self-referential (points to this code's own 2025 slot), not evidence of cross-code inheritance requiring D2 extraction. Crosswalk evidence is unusually clean for this batch: same code number retained across both KBLI-2020 and KBLI-2025 vintages ('Pemanenan kayu' -> 'Pemanenan Kayu'), confirmed by BOTH the forward (Lampiran 5) and reverse (Lampiran 10) BPS Vol.2 tables independently, with the surrounding rows on both pages showing the SPLIT/MERGE pattern for neighboring forestry codes that 02201 was specifically exempt from -- this is the positive-control case for what a genuine ONE_TO_ONE looks like versus the SPLIT-mapped-as-single-code failure mode the workflow doc warns against.

Independently read crosswalk/lampiran10_p329-329.png (reverse, KBLI2025->KBLI2020): row '02201 Pemanenan Kayu -> 02201 Pemanenan kayu' likewise appears as a single isolated row with no other inbound 2020 code -- unlike neighboring 02102 (6 inbound 2020 rows: 02111/02112/02113/02119/02121/02122) and 02300 (8 inbound rows: 02301-02309), which is exactly the SPLIT/MERGE contrast pattern the proposal cites as the surrounding-page positive-control evidence. This bidirectional isolation is genuine ONE_TO_ONE evidence, independently re-derived, not just asserted.

Read pp28/ABSENT.json myself: verdict='absent', 11,208 pages scanned across 21 source files (394930-394950), code 02201 not found -- matches proposal's ABSENT claim exactly (no fabricated file count).

Read oss/detail.json (not explicitly cited by D1 but load-bearing for the licensing_inherits=false claim): id_version='fff4053d-cbb0-51e9-9dc5-1e85b5740704', version='2025' -- the 'fff4053d' prefix matches canonical.json's _l1_source='OSS_RBA_2025_id_version_fff4053d' exactly, independently confirming the per_skala licensing block traces to a 2025-native OSS RBA record, not an inherited PP28-vintage table. This supports the proposal's argument that pp28_sources=['02201'] is self-referential rather than cross-code D2 inheritance evidence.

Title match is near-identical ('Pemanenan kayu' vs 'Pemanenan Kayu', capitalization only) on both pages, consistent with the proposal's framing that the match rests on uraian-level semantic identity plus title, not title alone.

No divergence found between my blind independent re-derivation and the D1 proposal on: mapping_type (ONE_TO_ONE), page/row citations (both PNGs verified to contain exactly the cited row), licensing_inherits (false), or confidence (high). All cited file paths and figures (page 135, page 329, 11,208 pages, 21 files, fff4053d) were verified to exist and match on disk in this turn -- no phantom citations detected.
